newsitem.title: FRANCE: Refineries squeezed as French fuel shortage widens.
newsitem.headline: Refineries squeezed as French fuel shortage widens.

text.p: Fuel shortages spread to nearly half France's petrol stations on Friday and refineries were said to be trimming production as truckers kept up a 12-day strike.
"All the refineries have reduced a little bit but it's not much," a spokeswoman for oil industry association UFIP said.
There was no immediate confirmation refinery operators.
The oil industry has warned of cuts in refinery production by the end of the week if truck drivers continue to barricade refineries and fuel depots in a protest over pay and conditions.
Industry ministry officials said on Friday that 8,000 of France's 18,000 petrol stations were short of fuel or out of stock and the number was rising.
"Unless the blockades are lifted at the depots, it has to rise very quickly and we could reach 10,000 this weekend," a senior ministry official told Reuters.
Industry ministry officials said they were also concerned about a separate strike by distribution workers at three Elf Aquitaine refineries on Wednesday and Thursday.
They were also worried about potentially disastrous consequences of the widepsread fuel shortage on farmers, especially poultry breeders.
"Poultry raisers are running out of domestic fuel oil and butane and propane," a ministry official said. "We risk seeing a massacre of chickens this weekend because of the cold."
The truck strike, in the crucial pre-Christmas period, is costing the food and haulage industries tens of millions of dollars a day, prompting protests from France's neighbours.
Unions said earlier they were keen to negotiate a solution provided the state guaranteed payment for all hours worked.
